definitions.explanation: Molten rock that flows from a volcano during an eruption, or the solidified rock formed when it cools.

examples.japanese: ⟦{火山|かざん}→火山：04020_kazan⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{溶岩|ようがん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流|なが}れ{出|だ}した→流れ出す：06086_nagaredasu⟧。
examples.english: Lava flowed out of the volcano.

examples.japanese: {溶岩|ようがん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{冷|ひ}えて→冷える：01154_hieru⟧⟦{固|かた}まった→固まる：01928_katamaru⟧⟦{岩|いわ}→岩：00850_iwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}られる→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: You can see rocks formed from cooled and solidified lava.

examples.japanese: ⟦{富士山|ふじさん}→富士山：09514_fujisan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{周辺|しゅうへん}→周辺：09896_shuuhen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{過去|かこ}→過去：00152_kako⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{噴火|ふんか}→噴火：00045_funka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{流|なが}れた→流れる：01969_nagareru⟧{溶岩|ようがん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{跡|あと}→跡：02174_ato⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Around Mt. Fuji, there are traces of lava that flowed from past eruptions.

notes:
USAGE:
The characters literally mean "melted rock" (⟦{溶|と}ける→溶ける：02302_tokeru⟧ + ⟦{岩|いわ}→岩：00850_iwa⟧). Refers to both the molten state during eruption and the solidified rock afterward. Japan has many active volcanoes, making this word relevant in geography, tourism, and disaster preparedness.

The underground version before eruption is called ⟦マグマ→マグマ：22084_maguma⟧ (magma).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {溶岩|ようがん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流|なが}れる→流れる：01969_nagareru⟧: lava flows
- {溶岩流|ようがんりゅう}: lava flow
- {溶岩|ようがん}{台地|だいち}: lava plateau
- {溶岩|ようがん}⟦ドーム→ドーム：24058_doomu⟧: lava dome
